gen-dafont-neon-gf-orienta: Glowing and vibrant, Neon draws every curve at a constant width, like stamped metal. Orienta follows with sans letters that breathe, their cases close in height, which is what makes the pair hang together.
gen-dafont-neon-gf-oxygen: Oxygen reads as a plain sans with open curves and a lowercase that nearly matches its capitals. And Neon above it keeps a marker-like line, so the two feel like one glowing idea in two volumes.
gen-dafont-neon-gf-parkinsans: Parkinsans stays crisp even when small. Neon's stamped-metal lowercase and open spacing glow above it, while the body's single stroke thickness keeps the text tidy underneath.
gen-dafont-neon-gf-pathway-extreme: Loud, glowing, nib-drawn letters up top. Pathway Extreme answers with stubby ascenders and a big x-height, and that tension between a wandering marker line and a sturdy, open body is the pair's strongest quality.
gen-dafont-neon-gf-preahvihear: Preahvihear reads as a plain sans with a lofty x-height and mouths that stay wide open. Neon is best at glowing, bent-paperclip display lines, while Preahvihear is best at carrying the text beneath them.
gen-dafont-neon-gf-prompt: Neon's most distinctive trait is a stroke that never varies between stems and connecting strokes, giving it a glowing, vibrant hum. Prompt, a plain sans with oversized small letters, settles in underneath.
gen-dafont-neon-gf-pt-sans-caption: Neon's round letters carry walls as heavy as its straight ones, which gives it a glowing, vibrant punch. And PT Sans Caption, a plain sans with big-bodied lowercase, lets that heading earn its keep when set big and short.
gen-dafont-neon-gf-puritan: Neon holds a monoweight stroke throughout, so its stamped-metal lowercase glows with a vibrant, uninterrupted line. Puritan, a plain sans with oversized e and a counters, keeps paragraphs inviting.
gen-dafont-neon-gf-questrial: Neon is all glow and stamped-metal swagger. It does best at loud, vibrant display lines, while Questrial, a plain sans cut from single-weight strokes, does its best work in quiet, flat-feeling text.
gen-dafont-neon-gf-radio-canada: Glowing letters, stamped and bold. Neon is best at drawing the eye with its open spacing and unvarying line, while Radio Canada is best at steady sans text with tall, full c, s and z.
